PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(DISQUALIFICATION FOR MEMBERSHIP) RULES, 1990
[Gazette of Pakistan,
Extraordinary, Part I, 20th August, 1990]
S.R.O. 866(1)/90, dated 20‑8‑1990.‑‑1n
exercise of the powers conferred by Article 11 of the Parliament and Provincial
Assemblies (Disqualification for Membership) Order, 1977 [P. (P.P.) O.No.17 of
1977], the Federal Government is pleased to make the following rules:‑‑
1. (1) These Rules may be
called the Parliament and Provincial Assemblies (Disqualification for
Membership) Rules, 1990.
(2) They shall come into force
at once.
2. In these rules, unless there
is anything repugnant in the subject or context.‑‑
(a) "Article" means
Article of the Order;
(b) "notice" means a
notice under paragraph (b) of clause (3) of Article 4;
(c) "Order" means the
Parliament and Provincial Assemblies (Disqualification for Membership) Order,
1977 [P.(P.P.) O.No.17 of 1977];
(d) "reference" means
a reference made by a referring authority to a Special Court; and
(e) "referring
authority" means the President, or as the case may be, the Governor.
3. The President may appoint
one or more persons to assist the Special Court in the scrutiny of records
under clause (3) of Article 4 and in the conduct of the enquiry under Article 5
and no such appointment shall be questioned.
4. A reference shall consist of
a concise statement of the material facts on which the referring authority is
satisfied that there are reasonable grounds for believing that an act of
misconduct has been committed by the respondent:
Provided that such reference
shall not preclude the referring authority from (i) submitting at any stage of
the proceedings such further material as may subsequently become available in
support of the act of misconduct to which the reference relates; or (ii) making
a reference with regard to any other act of misconduct on which the Special
Court has not expressed an opinion under paragraph (a) of clause (3) of Article
4. '
5. A notice shall be given to
the respondent in the form contained in the Schedule to these rules.
6. The Special Court shall not
merely by reason of a change in its composition be bound to recall or re‑examine
any witness who has given evidence prior to such change and may act on the
evidence already given or produced before it.
7. The Special Court shall
proceed with the enquiry from day to day and shall not adjourn any proceedings
for any purpose unless such adjournment is, in its opinion, necessary in the
interest of justice; and no adjournment shall be granted for more than two
days.
8. The Special Court shall have
power, without prejudice to any other powers which it may have to prohibit the
publication of the contents of any document connected with, or of any
information relating to any proceedings coming before it upon a reference.
9. (1) In proceedings under the
Order, the Special Court shall record evidence in such manner as appears to it
just and proper for the purpose of recording its findings.
(2) The respondent shall be
entitled to show cause against the charges and be a competent witness in his
own behalf and may make a statement on oath at any stage of the enquiry, and
the Special Court may, for the purpose of enabling him to explain any
circumstances appearing against him, question him accordingly at any stage of
the enquiry and he shall make reply, on oath or otherwise as he may elect:
Provided that, where he fails
or refuses to show cause or to answer any such questions or to explain any
facts appearing against him, in regard to which he is shown or in the opinion
of the Court can he reasonably believed to have personal knowledge, the Special
Court shall be entitled to draw an adverse presumption against him.
(3) The respondent, if he so
chooses, shall have the right to consult a legal practitioner for which he
shall make arrangements before the proceedings commence.
